subject: Sandbox evaluation — integration agenda, success gates, and API stitch plan
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@finlytics.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox evaluation — integration agenda, success gates, and API stitch plan

Hi Samantha / Oliver —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier today. As promised, summary below of the proposed sandbox evaluation and a focused integration agenda so we can validate success within 3 weeks. Please skim and confirm any adjustments before I send the calendar invite + Miro board.

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood streaming + tool-calling flows against Finlytics’ real-time reconciliation use case and ensure latency and token-cost targets can be met on your sample dataset.

Proposed success criteria (concrete / testable)
- End-to-end streaming ingestion -> inference -> webhook callback latency < 450ms p50 for the 1k req/day test pattern.
- Mean token unit cost under your target of $0.0025 for summary-first workload (we’ll instrument with token breakdowns).
- Tool-calling: successful retrieval from your proprietary ledger API in 95% of calls with correct context passed in function payloads.
- No more than 2 functional regressions on canonical prompt set (we’ll agree the set by Friday).

Integration agenda (owner / measurable outputs)
1) SDK & routes (Week 0–1) — Owner: Ben Carter
   - Integrate node/python SDK for streaming routes; shared SDK snippet + small sample app.
   - Deliverable: sample app that opens a streaming session and posts callbacks to your dev webhook (repo link in Drive).
2) Tool-calling adapter (Week 1) — Owner: Marissa Cole
   - Wire the on-call function that fetches ledger records; provide a mock adapter and then swap to your dev API.
   - Deliverable: tool adapter that returns canonical responses for test prompts.
3) Acceptance & metrics (Week 2) — Owner: Evelyn Hart
   - Run 3-day spike with your sample traffic; collect latency, token breakdown, and failure rates.
   - Deliverable: evaluation report (latency p50/p95, cost per token, failure taxonomy).

Timeline (target)
- Fri Apr 20: finalize prompt set and mutual action plan
- Mon Apr 23: SDK integration complete (dev webhook receiving stream chunks)
- Mon Apr 30: tool-calling wired against your dev API; first smoke tests
- Wed May 2: 72-hour spike concludes; report delivered by EOD May 3

Security & ops notes
- We’ll provide a short onboarding packet for your security team (SOC2 scoping, data retention options, and audit log samples).
- If you prefer a VPC connector for the dev run, flag this now and Ben will loop infra.

Next steps / asks of Finlytics
- Confirm the 3-week plan and the proposed success criteria by EOD Thu Apr 19.
- Share a dev webhook URL and API key for the tool-calling adapter by Mon Apr 23 (or we can use a temporary proxy).
- Point person for day-to-day technical questions (name + slack handle).

Attachments: I’ve attached a compact integration matrix and a simple SDK route diagram.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@finlytics.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver@finlytics.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 10:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sandbox evaluation — integration agenda, success gates, and API stitch plan

Evelyn —

Appreciate the concise plan. This aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Latency target: p50 < 450ms is fine for the streaming chunks, but can we also capture p95? Our enterprise SLA cares about tail latency.
2) Token costs: we'll provide the representative prompt/response sizes. If you can include a quick sensitivity table (tokens vs cost) that would help our finance partner.
3) Tool-calling adapter: our dev API requires a bearer token and a client cert; can you support a cert-based mock adapter or should we spin up a short-lived service that accepts cert pinning?

We can confirm the dev webhook and credentials by Mon Apr 23. Day-to-day tech lead will be me (samantha.reed on Slack). Procurement will loop in approval shortly after we finalize success criteria.

Two minor asks: please add p95 to the acceptance metrics and include an initial rollback/fallback policy (e.g., non-blocking fallback to batch mode if tool-calls exceed X% failure rate).

If that all sounds good I’ll approve the schedule and we’ll aim to kick off Apr 23.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Reed
Head of Integrations | Finlytics
samantha.reed@finlytics.ai | +1 (617) 555-0987

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Finlytics — certs, p95, and fallback plan (prep for kickoff)

Team — quick internal note after Samantha’s response. Action items below so we can be ready for Mon Apr 23 kickoff.

Action items
- Ben: please prepare an infra note on supporting client certs for the mock adapter and whether we need a short-lived proxy. Also include steps for enabling VPC connector if they request it (estimate work days).
- Marissa: add a rollback/fallback policy to the tool-calling design. Suggestion: if tool-call failures > 10% over a 5-min window, switch to batched reconciliation mode and flag alerts.
- Evelyn: I’ll add p95 to the acceptance report and create a token sensitivity table for Samantha.

Attachments: I’ve dropped a draft fallback policy in Drive (mutual-action-plan-FT.docx).

Ben / Marissa — can you reply with ETA for your items by EOD Thu Apr 18? I’ll reconcile and send the final MAP to Finlytics on Fri Apr 19.

Thanks —
Evelyn

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@finlytics.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@finlytics.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox evaluation — integration agenda, success gates, and API stitch plan

Hi Samantha / Oliver —

Thanks — confirmed on the three asks. Quick callouts to what we updated in the attached MAP before kickoff:
- Acceptance metrics now include p50 and p95 latency (we’ll report both) and a token sensitivity table attached.
- Fallback policy: automatic non-blocking switch to batched mode if tool-calls exceed 10% failure over a 5-minute window; will surface immediate PagerDuty alert and create a rollback ticket.
- Client cert support: Ben confirmed we can support a cert-based mock adapter; if you prefer we can host a short-lived proxy and manage certs for the dev run.

Next steps:
- I’ve scheduled a 30-min kickoff for Mon Apr 23 at 09:00 PT (invite sent to your team).
- Please share the dev webhook + cert details via the secure Drive upload we shared OR use the temporary proxy link by Mon Apr 23 08:00 PT.

Attachments: redwood-integration-matrix.xlsx, sdk-route-diagram.png, mutual-action-plan-FT.docx

Looking forward to working with you — we’ll also introduce our CS contact on the kickoff to ensure smooth evaluation and procurement alignment.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Evelyn.hart@redwood.com
